data.name: Jonan
data.gender_notes: Jonan is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jonan is a Hebrew name with the meaning 'God is gracious'. It is derived from the Hebrew word 'yonah', which means 'dove'. In the Bible, Jonah is the name of a prophet who was swallowed by a whale and then miraculously saved. The name Jonan carries the meaning “God is gracious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Jonan usually hope their child will grow to embody god is gracious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes God's grace, mercy, and protection.
data.etymology: Jonan belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is gracious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jonan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_latin.name: Ionan

in_english.name: Jonan

data.cultural_impact: The name Jonan carries a rich cultural heritage, as it is rooted in the ancient Hebrew tradition. It is a reminder of the deep connection between the Jewish people and their faith in God's graciousness and mercy. The name Jonan continues to be popular among Christians, particularly those with Hebrew or Jewish heritage, as a reminder of God's faithfulness and love.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jonan holds significant spiritual meaning for Christians. It is a reminder of the grace and mercy of God, who is always with us, even in the darkest moments of our lives. As the name Jonah in the Bible illustrates, even when we stray from God, He is always ready to welcome us back with open arms. The name Jonan encourages us to trust in God's grace and mercy, and to live our lives in a way that reflects His love and compassion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: There is no Christian name specifically called "Jonan" in the Bible. The closest name is "Jonah," which means "dove" in Hebrew, symbolizing God's protection and deliverance.

The name 'Johannes' is the Latin form of 'Jonan', and it was common during this time period for monks to adopt Latin names.

In the New Testament of the Bible, a man named Jonas is described as being a prophet who was commanded by God to go to the city of Nineveh and warn its inhabitants to repent of their sins. Jonas initially resisted this calling, but eventually obeyed and was successful in convincing Nineveh to repent. This story is a popular one in Christian tradition, and the name 'Jonan' is believed to have originated from this biblical figure.
